117. Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II

Given a binary tree

struct Node {
  int val;
  Node *left;
  Node *right;
  Node *next;
}

Populate each next pointer to point to its next right node. If there is no next right node, the next pointer should be set to NULL.

Initially, all next pointers are set to NULL.
input_format: A serialized level-order traversal array of a binary tree.
output_format: A serialized level-order traversal array where each level ends with a null.
explanation: Use the existing next pointers to traverse the current level; build the next level's links by following prev.next and child pointers.
